source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which part of a sterile surgical gown is considered sterile?
options: Front from chest to table level
questions.rationale: Gowns are sterile in front from chest to sterile field level and sleeves 2 inches above elbow to cuff.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Asepsis (PDF p. 487)
questions.quote: Gowns of the surgical team are considered sterile in front from the chest to the level of the sterile field

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A sterile package's integrity is doubtful. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Items of doubtful sterility are considered unsterile.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Asepsis (PDF p. 487)
questions.quote: Items of doubtful sterility are considered unsterile.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which part of a draped table is considered sterile?
questions.rationale: Only the top surface of a draped table is sterile.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Asepsis (PDF p. 487)
questions.quote: Only the top surface of a draped table is considered sterile.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which process destroys all microorganisms including spores?
questions.rationale: Sterilization is the highest level; boiling and pasteurization do not kill all spores.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sterilization (PDF p. 488)
questions.quote: Process in which all pathogens are destroyed including spores

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is the most common sterilization method in hospitals?
questions.rationale: Steam autoclave at 121°C is most common.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sterilization Methods (PDF p. 488)
questions.quote: Most common method

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Heat- and moisture-sensitive items are sterilized with:
questions.rationale: Ethylene oxide is used for heat-labile items.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sterilization Methods (PDF p. 488)
questions.quote: Ethylene oxide gas is used to sterilize items that are sensitive to heat or moisture

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Under Spaulding's classification, a vaginal speculum is:
questions.rationale: Semi-critical items contact mucous membranes and need high-level disinfection.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Spaulding's Classification (PDF p. 488)
questions.quote: Speculum

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A urinary catheter is classified as which Spaulding category?
questions.rationale: Critical items enter sterile tissue or body cavities and must be sterile.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Spaulding's Classification (PDF p. 488)
questions.quote: Urinary catheter, needles

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During which stage of general anesthesia may the client have uncontrolled movements requiring restraint?
questions.rationale: Stage 2 (excitement): dilated pupils, rapid pulse, irregular breathing, movement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stages of Anesthesia (PDF p. 489)
questions.quote: Because of uncontrolled movement of the patient, restraints are necessary

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Shallow respirations, weak pulse, and widely dilated pupils during anesthesia indicate:
questions.rationale: Stage 4 medullary depression; stop anesthesia and support breathing and circulation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stages of Anesthesia (PDF p. 489)
questions.quote: Too much anesthesia has been administered

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Spinal anesthesia is usually injected into the subarachnoid space at:
questions.rationale: Usually between L4 and L5, anesthetizing lower extremities, perineum, lower abdomen.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Spinal Anesthesia (PDF p. 490)
questions.quote: usually between L4 and L5

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: If hair must be removed before surgery, the nurse uses:
questions.rationale: Clippers reduce skin injury and infection risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Preparation (PDF p. 491)
questions.quote: If hair must be removed, electric clippers are used

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client refuses to remove her wedding ring before surgery. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: If the client objects, secure the ring with tape per policy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Immediate Pre-op (PDF p. 491)
questions.quote: If the patient objects in removing wedding ring, secure it with tape

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After preoperative sedation is given, the nurse should:
options: Raise side rails, keep in bed
questions.rationale: Client voids before premedication; then stays in bed with rails up.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Immediate Pre-op (PDF p. 491)
questions.quote: If preanesthetic medication is administered, the patient is kept in bed with the side rails raised

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which position is used for hemorrhoidectomy?
questions.rationale: Kraske position elevates the hips for rectal procedures.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Positions (PDF p. 491)
questions.quote: Done for rectal procedures (pilonidal sinus, hemorrhoidectomy)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which surgical position is used for vaginal and perineal procedures?
questions.rationale: Lithotomy for perineal, vaginal, urologic, and rectal procedures.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Positions (PDF p. 491)
questions.quote: Used for perineal, vaginal, urologic and rectal procedures

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which measure prevents intraoperative hypothermia?
questions.rationale: Warm fluids, remove wet drapes, and adjust room temperature.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypothermia (PDF p. 492)
questions.quote: Warm IV and irrigating fluids

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which scissors are used to cut delicate tissue?
questions.rationale: Metzenbaum is delicate; Mayo cuts heavy fascia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Scissors (PDF p. 492)
questions.quote: Metzenbaum scissors are more delicate than mayo scissors

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which forceps grasp delicate structures like the fallopian tube without injury?
questions.rationale: Babcock jaws are rounded for atraumatic grasping.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Grasping Forceps (PDF p. 493)
questions.quote: Babcock Forceps- end of each jaw is rounded to grasp tissue without injury

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which suture gains tensile strength when wet?
questions.rationale: Cotton gains strength when wet; silk loses it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sutures (PDF p. 493)
questions.quote: Gains tensile strength when wet

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which needle point is used for friable tissues like the liver?
questions.rationale: Blunt points suture friable tissue; cutting points for skin and tendon.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgical Needles (PDF p. 493)
questions.quote: Blunt point is used for suturing friable tissues such as liver and kidney

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which Aldrete score usually allows discharge from the PACU?
questions.rationale: Score 8–10 (activity, respiration, circulation, consciousness, SpO2).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, PACU Discharge (PDF p. 494)
questions.quote: Aldrete score is usually 8 to 10 before discharge from the PACU

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the PACU nurse's first assessment priority?
questions.rationale: Maintain airway and respiratory function first.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, PACU Management (PDF p. 494)
questions.quote: Assess patient’s airway, respiratory function

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Protrusion of abdominal organs through a wound opening is:
questions.rationale: Evisceration is protrusion of viscera; dehiscence is separation of wound edges.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Wound Complications (PDF p. 494)
questions.quote: EVISCERATION- Protrusion of viscera through an abnormal wound opening
